newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver jumps up on poor supply, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver jumps up on poor supply, gold steady.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closes 80 rupees higher at 7,605 rupees per kg on poor arrivals and shortage of ready stock.
** Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees higher at 4,890 rupees per 10 gramme on seasonal buying and lower than expected arrivals while prices in global markets remained firm.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) closed 100 rupees higher at 57,200 rupees per piece. They were up 200 rupees on Wednesday.
Silver (.999) closed 80 rupees higher at 7,605 rupees per kg on speculative buying following an uptrend in prices in world markets and shortage of ready stock, dealers said.
Silver was up 15 rupees per kg on Wednesday. "Industrial buying however remained low ahead of the budget scheduled for Friday but speculators remained active buyers during the day," they said.
Finance minister P.Chidambaram presents his second budget on Friday.
Gold 24 carat ended 10 rupees higher at 4,890 rupees per 10 gramme on fresh seasonal buying while arrivals were lower than expected, dealers said.
Gold was up by 10 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday.
"Today gold actually opened steady despite uptrend in the world market but later on moved up along with the recovery in silver prices and ended higher," one dealer said.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) ended 100 rupees higher at 57,200 rupees per piece after gaining 200 rupees on Wednesday.
They were up 1,100 rupees per piece last week.
